newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia Rosgosstrakh to be sold as planned - Kokh.
newsitem.headline: Russia Rosgosstrakh to be sold as planned - Kokh.

text.p: Russia's largest insurance company, OAO Rosgosstrakh, will be privatised according to the original scheme, even if there are changes to legislation, privatisation minister Alfred Kokh said on Thursday.
"Unfortunately, even if we exclude the shortcomings (of legislation), this does not concern Rosgosstrakh, because it is well know that our laws have no retroactive force," he told a news conference.

On Tuesday Russia's lower house, the State Duma, said it had prepared a resolution appealing to President Boris Yeltsin to draw up a new privatisation plan for the insurer, replacing the current scheme.
The Duma said Rosgosstrakh had to have a special privatisation scheme covered by a special federal law, which it wants the government to present to the Duma by July 1.
Under the current privatisation scheme employees bought 20 percent of Rosgosstrakh shares and a nine-member buy-out team has a priority right to 30 percent.
The remaining 50 percent would be put up for a cash auction this year.
